summary:
### TL;DR
- **CodeQL 2.27.3 has a breaking change for GitHub Actions analysis.** The Actions control flow graph now uses the shared CFG library, and the legacy `Completion` classes are gone. If you maintain custom CodeQL queries for workflows, check them. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-codeql-2-27-3-adds-python-3-15-features-and-json-data-extensions))
- **CodeQL 2.27.3 adds detection features:**
  - An opt-in `ai` threat model for LLM-generated data.
  - JSON syntax for data extensions.
  - Python 3.15 support.
  - Several false-positive reductions. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-codeql-2-27-3-adds-python-3-15-features-and-json-data-extensions))
- **Dependabot can now keep AI agent dependencies up to date.** It supports version updates for Agent Package Manager (`apm.yml`), but not security updates. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-dependabot-version-updates-support-agent-package-manager))
- **The Copilot usage metrics API now separates BYOK usage.** You can see local BYOK and enterprise custom model usage on their own, which supports BYOK policy governance. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-byok-and-enterprise-custom-models-in-the-copilot-usage-api))

### Action required
- **Custom CodeQL queries for GitHub Actions may break.** This applies if your queries rely on specific CFG nodes, edges, or basic block boundaries.
  - Replace the removed `Completion` classes with CFG edge labels such as `DirectSuccessor`, `BooleanSuccessor`, and `ReturnSuccessor`.
  - The change is already deployed automatically to code scanning on github.com.
  - For GHES, it ships in 3.24. Older GHES versions get it if you manually upgrade CodeQL.
  - No specific deadline was given.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-codeql-2-27-3-adds-python-3-15-features-and-json-data-extensions))

### Security improvements
- **CodeQL 2.27.3** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-codeql-2-27-3-adds-python-3-15-features-and-json-data-extensions)):
  - **New `ai` threat model:** an opt-in model for LLM-generated data. It has no built-in sources, so you define your own sources through data extensions.
  - **Python query sources:** `py/xxe`, `py/xml-bomb`, and `py/nosql-injection` now respect your configured threat model and include sources you model with data extensions. By default they still use remote flow sources.
  - **Java/Kotlin false-positive fixes:** `java/ssrf` and `java/unvalidated-url-redirection` now recognize case-insensitive `URI.getHost()` allowlist checks, including when the host is stored in a local variable.
  - **Ruby:** `Grape::API` request sub-accessors are now treated as remote flow sources.
  - **C#:** with private registries, CodeQL now passes the required proxy and certificate environment variables to the NuGet CLI.
- **Dependabot and APM:** Dependabot now opens PRs for supported git dependencies in `apm.yml` and regenerates `apm.lock.yaml` when present. It is generally available on github.com and coming in GHES 3.24. To enable it, add an `apm` entry to `.github/dependabot.yml`. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-dependabot-version-updates-support-agent-package-manager))
- **Dependabot and Python 3.15:** projects upgraded to Python 3.15 keep receiving Dependabot updates. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-dependabot-now-supports-python-3-15))
- **BYOK visibility in the Copilot usage metrics API** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-byok-and-enterprise-custom-models-in-the-copilot-usage-api)):
  - New fields: `used_local_byok`, `totals_by_local_byok`, active local BYOK user counts, and `is_custom_enterprise_model`.
  - These let you audit who sends requests to their own provider keys or local models.
  - Local BYOK figures rely on client telemetry and are a lower bound: they undercount when telemetry is disabled.
  - There is no backfill for earlier report days.
- **Copilot cloud tasks in JetBrains Air** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-03-github-copilot-is-now-available-in-jetbrains-air)):
  - Each task runs in a Docker container on a fresh VM, with all traffic going through a proxy and no state carried between tasks.
  - Air's governance and analytics features do not include Copilot usage.
  - Air admins can disable Copilot but cannot set Copilot spending limits within Air.

### Docs changes worth reading
- **Configuring Dependabot security updates:** the docs no longer say that, on public repositories, the Enable/Disable button is disabled because the feature is always on.
  - The commit title says it corrects docs that claimed dependency graph and Dependabot alerts are on by default for public repos.
  - Don't assume these features are enabled automatically on public repos. Verify them in each repository's Code security settings.
  - ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/5d9f6a98825dc0e3c2f93d42e43f9e0ef819450d), [page](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/secure-your-dependencies/configure-security-updates))

changelog.title: BYOK and enterprise custom models in the Copilot usage API
changelog.text: The Copilot usage metrics API now shows bring your own key (BYOK) usage across GitHub Copilot, so you can separate it from Copilot-hosted model usage. Reports cover two kinds of BYOK: Local BYOK is configured by developers in their client. Requests go from Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app directly to the developer’s provider key or local model. Find it in used_local_byok , totals_by_local_byok , and active local BYOK user counts. Enterprise custom models are configured by admins in GitHub settings, and requests route through GitHub to your provider. Find them with is_custom_enterprise_model in totals_by_client . Both appear in enterprise and organization reports, at the user and aggregate level, in 1-day and 28-day reports. Local BYOK Local BYOK covers a developer’s own provider key and local models served by tools such as Ollama, Foundry Local, LM Studio, and llama-server. used_local_byok : Whether a user made at least one local BYOK request in Copilot CLI or the Copilot app that day. Appears in user-level reports. totals_by_local_byok : Session, request, prompt, and token counts, broken out by byok_kind ( local_managed , local_user , local_auto , or remote_user ) and surface ( copilot_cli or copilot_app ). Appears in user-level and aggregate reports. daily_active_local_byok_users , weekly_active_local_byok_users , and monthly_active_local_byok_users : Distinct users with local BYOK activity for the day, calendar week, and calendar month. Appears in aggregate reports. Enterprise custom models Added is_custom_enterprise_model , a boolean on each totals_by_client[].totals_by_model[] entry. Its value is true when the request used a custom model configured for your enterprise or organization. GitHub observes these requests server-side, so the field covers every client, including IDEs. A model used both as a Copilot-hosted model and as a custom model appears as two entries, so the counts stay separate. Custom model entries include real request and token counts. Why this matters BYOK usage used to blend into Copilot-hosted totals, because local and custom models often share names with Copilot models. Now you can: Govern BYOK: See who sends requests to their own provider keys, local models, or enterprise custom models, and check that against your BYOK policy. Understand spend: Separate Copilot-hosted usage from usage billed by your own provider or run on free local models, so cost per user reflects what Copilot actually serves. See across all tools: Get one view of AI usage in your enterprise, whichever model or provider your developers choose. Compare efficiency: Group users by BYOK or custom model usage and compare them against the Copilot usage metrics you already track. Important notes No change to existing totals: BYOK usage is already counted. Local BYOK is a subset of totals_by_cli and totals_by_copilot_app , and custom model usage is already in totals_by_client . Existing totals are unchanged. Lower bound for local BYOK: Local BYOK fields rely on client telemetry, so they undercount when telemetry is disabled. Token counts can also undercount because some local providers don’t report token usage. Enterprise custom model counts are observed server-side and don’t have this limitation. Model names: Custom model names use the existing model name normalization, so unrecognized names appear as unknown . Local BYOK usage isn’t broken out by model name. No backfill: Report days before this release don’t include is_custom_enterprise_model . Access: Available to enterprise owners, enterprise billing managers, organization owners, and anyone with a custom organization or enterprise role that grants the View Copilot Metrics permission. The Copilot usage metrics policy must be enabled. Visit the Copilot usage metrics API documentation to get started. The post BYOK and enterprise custom models in the Copilot usage API appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Dependabot version updates support Agent Package Manager
changelog.text: You can now keep your AI agent skills, prompts, and instructions up to date with Dependabot version updates for Agent Package Manager (APM) . Dependabot opens pull requests to update supported git dependencies declared in apm.yml and regenerates apm.lock.yaml when it’s present. This support covers version updates, not security updates. Get started Add an apm entry to your .github/dependabot.yml file, specify the directory containing apm.yml , and choose an update schedule. APM support is generally available on github.com for all GitHub plans and will be available in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24. Learn more Configuring Dependabot version updates Supported APM dependencies and update behavior Community discussion on APM support The post Dependabot version updates support Agent Package Manager appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot is now available in JetBrains Air
changelog.text: You can now delegate coding tasks, guide execution, and review results with GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air . The integration uses the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) and supports tasks in your JetBrains IDE or in the cloud. Use Copilot in Air alongside the GitHub Copilot plugin and choose the workflow that works best for you. For a comparison and FAQ, see GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air . What’s new GitHub Copilot in Air’s agent picker : Select GitHub Copilot and use your existing Copilot subscription for coding tasks. Parallel work and in-context review : Track multiple agent sessions, use project context and IDE tools, and review changes alongside your code. Cloud tasks on your GitHub Copilot subscription : Run Copilot in isolated cloud environments through Air Teams, from your IDE or browser. Tasks use your Copilot plan rather than JetBrains AI credits. Get started For local tasks, install Air in your JetBrains IDE , select GitHub Copilot , and connect your GitHub Copilot account. For cloud tasks, you’ll need a JetBrains account in an Air Teams-enabled business organization, a GitHub Copilot subscription, and Copilot enabled by your Air administrator. There are two ways to run cloud tasks: Browser : Open Air in your browser , connect GitHub under Settings > VCS Providers , and create a task. Choose your repository and remote branch, select GitHub Copilot , and send your prompt. IDE : Use the Air plugin in your JetBrains IDE and select Cloud from the environment selector. Where Copilot cloud tasks run When you run a GitHub Copilot cloud task through JetBrains Air, Copilot works in a Docker container on a fresh virtual machine. All traffic passes through a proxy, and no state carries over between tasks. Copilot can build, test, and install packages without modifying your local environment. For more information, see Cloud agent sandboxing in Air . Cloud task considerations Subscription checks : Connecting GitHub Copilot to Air does not request GitHub Copilot permissions. Air may only verify subscription or credit availability when the cloud environment starts. If your subscription or credits are unavailable, the task fails and an error appears in the session. Plan selection : You cannot choose whether an individual task uses your personal GitHub Copilot plan or your organization’s plan. Usage visibility : Air’s governance and analytics features do not include Copilot usage. Administrative controls : Air administrators can disable GitHub Copilot through a governance policy, but cannot set Copilot spending limits within Air. Share your feedback Share your thoughts through in-product feedback, our feedback repository , or the private survey . The post GitHub Copilot is now available in JetBrains Air appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: CodeQL 2.27.3 adds Python 3.15 features and JSON data extensions
changelog.text: CodeQL is the static analysis engine behind GitHub code scanning, which finds and remediates security issues in your code. We’ve recently released CodeQL 2.27.3 . It supports new Python 3.15 language features, adds JSON syntax for data extensions, adds C23 bit-precise integers, and includes accuracy improvements across languages. Language and framework support CodeQL CLI Data extension files now support JSON syntax, using the same structure as YAML data extensions. Java-style comments ( // ... and /* ... */ ) also work. CodeQL parses files with the .json extension as JSON and continues to parse all other files as YAML. We’ve added an opt-in ai threat model for LLM-generated data. It doesn’t include any built-in source models, so you can define your own sources with data extensions. Python The Python extractor now supports Python 3.15 syntax, including unary plus in match literal patterns and Unicode 17 identifiers. We’ve added support for the new frozendict and sentinel builtins introduced in Python 3.15, including data flow modeling for frozendict construction. C/C++ We’ve added support for C23 bit-precise integers ( _BitInt(N) ). We’ve added flow summaries for the BlazingMQ BloombergLP::bmqa::Message and MessageProperties classes and their iterators. C# We’ve added support for data flow through positional patterns in is expressions and switch cases. When you configure private registries, CodeQL now passes the required proxy and certificate environment variables to the NuGet CLI. Ruby CodeQL now treats Grape::API request sub-accessors as remote flow sources. These include body.read , body.string , params , GET , POST , cookies , env , query_string , and path_info . Query changes C/C++ The cpp/resource-not-released-in-destructor query now recognizes resources released through local aliases, reducing false positives. C# The cs/simplifiable-boolean-expression query now produces fewer false positives when type information is incomplete. Java/Kotlin The java/ssrf and java/unvalidated-url-redirection queries now recognize case-insensitive comparisons of URI.getHost() with fixed allowlist entries. They also recognize these checks when code stores the host in a local variable, which reduces false positives. Python The py/xxe , py/xml-bomb , and py/nosql-injection queries now respect your configured threat model when selecting untrusted data sources. By default, they still use remote flow sources. These queries now also include sources you model with data extensions. Breaking changes GitHub Actions: The GitHub Actions control flow graph (CFG) now uses the shared CFG library. If your custom queries rely on specific CFG nodes, edges, or basic block boundaries, you may need to update them. We’ve removed the legacy Completion classes, so use CFG edge labels such as DirectSuccessor , BooleanSuccessor , and ReturnSuccessor instead. For a full list of changes, please refer to the complete changelog for version 2.27.3 . Every new version of CodeQL is automatically deployed to users of GitHub code scanning on github.com. The new functionality in CodeQL 2.27.3 will also be included in GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) 3.24 release. If you use an older version of GHES, you can manually upgrade your CodeQL version . The post CodeQL 2.27.3 adds Python 3.15 features and JSON data extensions appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Dependabot now supports Python 3.15
changelog.text: You can now upgrade your projects to Python 3.15 and keep receiving Dependabot updates. Support for Python 3.15 is available to all github.com users and will be included in GitHub Enterprise Server 3.24. For the full list of ecosystems that Dependabot supports, see Dependabot supported ecosystems and repositories . The post Dependabot now supports Python 3.15 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
